english.title: Failure to notify the petroleum enforcement authority before ceasing to occupy dispensing premises
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being a person who was keeping petrol on dispensing premises, namely **(..SPECIFY PREMISES..), in respect of which there was a storage certificate, failed to notify the petroleum enforcement authority in accordance with regulation 9 of the Petroleum (Consolidation) Regulations 2014, before ceasing to occupy those premises
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 4, 5 and 9 of the Petroleum (Consolidation) Regulations 2014 and section 33(1)(c) and schedule 3A to the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974.

english.notes:
(i) A notification must be made in writing and state -

(a) the person's name and address;
(b) the address of the dispensing premises; and (c) the date on which the person proposes to cease occupation of the dispensing premises.

(ii) The notification must be given -

(a) a maximum of six months; and (b) a minimum of 28 days,

before the day on which the person ceases to occupy the dispensing premises.

(iii) A contravention of paragraph (3)(b) does not relieve a person from the duty to notify the petroleum enforcement authority under paragraphs (1) and (2).

other.penalty:
Either Way -

Summary: Maximum 12 months imprisonment / or a fine
Indictment: Maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes:
In relation to an offence committed before section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
